correctness.rationale: Standard Haar step integrations give exactly 2^{-k}phi(2^k x)^2. Jordan derivative-measure representation plus Hilbert Minkowski gives the sharp operator norm and equality-case rigidity. At s=0 exact Parseval yields x(1-x). For s>0 a dyadic-rational perturbation has strictly larger energy than midpoint. The pointwise calibrated coboundary identity proves the infinite-horizon upper bound, with the orbit 1/3↔2/3 giving its leading lower bound; the discounted invariance equation identifies the unique limiting occupation measure. Divergence at s≥1/2 follows from a single step. The included exact-rational checker verifies finite formulas, not infinite statements.

value.rationale: The natural sharp BV-to-weighted-Haar Hilbert embedding has two exact functional thresholds: change of extremizing jump geometry at s=0 and loss of finite norm at s=1/2. Its critical coefficient 1/9, strictly lower than the independent-level envelope 1/4, quantifies genuine multiscale compatibility; orbit-measure rigidity identifies the scale distribution of near-critical worst jumps. This is an intrinsic spectral approximation/variation benchmark rather than an arbitrary finite lookup.
